newsitem.title: SINGAPORE: India's Bharat Petroleum restarts crude unit.
newsitem.headline: India's Bharat Petroleum restarts crude unit.

text.p: SINGAPORE, Feb 6 (SIngapore) - Indian state refiner Bharat Petroleum Corporation Ltd restarted its 6 million tonne-per-year (120,000-barrel-per-day) crude distillation unit (CDU) after a 29 day shutdown, a company source said on Thursday.
He said the turnaround at the Bombay refinery was routine after its last shutdown around 36 months ago.
One of BPCL's two crackers, a 900,000 tonne-per-year (18,000-bpd) unit had also been shutdown January 9, and was due to restart February 15.
The source said the other smaller cracker at 600,000 tonne-per-year (12,000-bpd) is tentatively scheduled to shutdown in May for 30-35 days.
The shutdowns did not create any major product shortfall as the refiner was prepared and "had already accounted for it".
